newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen moving up on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen moving up on Wall Street.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to move up in early Tuesday on further foreign buying of blue-chip counters following a sharp rise in Wall Street overnight, brokers said.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed at another record high on Monday, as Wall Street bet that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged at a policy-setting meeting next week.
"News of unchanged interest rate in the U.S. will push buying interest among foreign buyers. As usual they will target blue chip counters," one broker with local firm said.
The broker said he believed increased foreign buying interest would give local investors the confidence to buy medium and small-capped stocks.
"Speculative buying on Bayu Buana issue is likely to continue today," broker Suharto of Bhakti Investama said.
Travel and tourism firm Bayu Buana was active on Monday due to market talk that the firm was a target of a takeover. Company officials were not available for comment.
Further local-led buying was expected in supermarket Hero and its unit Suba Indah due to fundamentals.
"The interest is linked to recent reports that Hero was unlikely to be affected by the government policy to stop big supermarkets and retailers from expanding to small towns," one broker said.
Big-caps Telkom, Semen Cibinong and Citra Marga were among the losers following the profit-taking, brokers said.
Telkom fell 50 rupiah to 3,775 rupiah albeit in small volume.
Property firms Elang Realty, Modern Land and Jakarta International Hotels dominated the active list due mostly to local speculative buying, brokers said.

"Modern Land posted poor net profit last year. It is unlikely to post strong results this year. But continued talk of a possible link-up with a foreign firm boosted sentiment on the issue," another broker said.
Modern Land posted a net profit of 14.2 billion rupiah in 1996 against 23.0 billion rupiah in 1995.
Modern Land rose 225 rupiah to 3,925 rupiah, with some five million shares traded.
